clauses.reason: The command is "I hereby continue in effect until and including April 1, 1953, all appointments as officers and as warrant officers of the Army and of the Air Force" that would otherwise terminate in the stated window under the three listed provisions. The order's own words fix the last day as April 1, 1953, inclusive. No held order revokes, extends or amends it, so this is the first end. State on 2026-10-14: terminated.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory splits the order into three clauses that are only the enumerated statutory provisions (1), (2) and (3) and omits the command that governs them. The operative command is the whole sentence beginning 'By virtue of the authority' and running through item (3): it continues in effect until and including April 1, 1953 the listed appointments of Army and Air Force officers and warrant officers.

research_rationale:
EO 10397 (17 FR 8605; signed September 25, 1952; F.R. Doc. 52-10565) continues in effect, under section 1(c) of the Emergency Powers Continuation Act (66 Stat. 333), "until and including April 1, 1953" all appointments as officers and warrant officers of the Army and Air Force that would terminate after April 27, 1952 and before April 1, 1953 under three listed provisions of law. The first end is the own-terms date April 1, 1953. The order says 'until and including', so the date is inclusive by the order's own words. No exclusive reading is needed. The end source is the held Federal Register text of the order itself (the order's registered original); the packet's wording leads for this order come from a text without a graded fragment record and are not used.
